title: The Slave Pens
body: The Slave Pens lie beneath Serpent Lake in Coilfang Reservoir, a maze of flooded tunnels where the naga keep their slaves. Wastewalker Broken toil here as workers under Coilfang slavehandlers, who slap them and berate them for slacking off, while captives held apart in the pens call for help and asking how anyone can just leave them there. Not every Broken is a captive: Coilfang collaborators stand armed among the naga. Naga technicians, defenders, enchantresses and soothsayers hold the tunnels, observers patrol with rays at heel, and bogstroks swarm the shallows. Deeper in, the pens have masters of their own, and a few stand out even among the naga. Somewhere in the reservoir, too, are the druids the Cenarion Expedition is still waiting for.

parts.body: A bogstrok of monstrous size, Rokmar the Crackler, held a stretch of the pens as its own and met intruders in the shallows with its great claws. It fell there, among the lesser bogstroks of the pens.

title: Mennu the Betrayer
body: Mennu the Betrayer is a Broken, and he fights for the naga of Coilfang in the Slave Pens while others of his kind toil around him as slaves. His name says all that anyone is told of how he came to be there. He is a shaman, and he has kept the craft for his new masters: he sets down totems that bind his foes in grasping earth, harden his own skin against their blows and burst in searing novas, raises a ward to heal himself when hard pressed, and strikes at those who come for him with bolts of lightning.

parts.body: For all his totems and his lightning, Mennu fell in the Slave Pens, struck down among the naga he served while Broken slaves toiled around him. Whatever had turned him against his own people, he took the answer with him.

title: Quagmirran
body: Quagmirran is a fungal giant, and it keeps a lair deep in the Slave Pens, past the naga and their slaves. It does not wait to be found. When intruders step into its lair, the giant stirs and comes lumbering out along its path to meet them. It fights with crushing blows, cleaving at those before it and hurling them back with great uppercuts, and it fouls the air around it, spraying acid on one foe after another and loosing volleys of poison bolts over all who stand near.

parts.body: Not everyone believes Quagmirran is real. Naturalist Bite came into the Slave Pens to prove the existence of the giant, most mythical of fungal giants, and ended up shut in a naga cage not far from its lair. He got his wish, he admits, sort of.
sources: npc_text 9119 (gossip 7520: I came in here to prove the existence of Quagmirran, that most mythical of fungal giants. I got my wish, sort of.)

parts.body: Quagmirran came lumbering out to meet its killers and died in the Slave Pens, for all its crushing blows, its acid and its poison. The fungal giant that kept its lair past the naga and their slaves would trouble no one again.

title: Lost in Action
body: At the entrance to Coilfang Reservoir, Watcher Jhang begs for help. Ysiel Windsinger sent her and four companions to investigate the mystery of the steam pumps and why they are being used to drain the marsh, but her friends split up and went on recklessly without her. Those four can be such jerks sometimes, she says, but she loves them anyway, and she fears the worst. Their names are Earthbinder Rayge, Naturalist Bite, Weeder Greenthumb and Windcaller Claw, and they are to be sought in both the Slave Pens and the Underbog.

parts.body: Weeder Greenthumb did not make it out. His remains lie in the Slave Pens, where by all appearances he was killed quick and clean while trying to make his escape, one of Jhang's companions who would not be coming back.
sources: npc_text 9118 (gossip 7519: the remains of Weeder Greenthumb; killed quick and clean while trying to make his escape from the Slave Pens)

parts.body: Jhang was glad that some of her friends yet lived, though what had befallen the others broke her heart. At least, she sighed, they had died doing what they loved most in life, and she pressed a token of her eternal gratitude on the one who had brought her word.

title: The Cudgel of Kar'desh
body: In a cell in the Slave Pens the naga keep a prisoner of their own kind: Skar'this the Heretic. He has nothing but hatred for his jailers. Burn it all down, he rages: they deserve nothing, and they must pay for what they have done and for what they continue to do. He would kill Lady Vashj himself if he could break free of these bindings. Perhaps, he suggests to the soft-skin before him, they seek to do the work of Neptulon; either way her death serves them both, and together they might form the sacred cudgel.

parts.body: The cudgel of Kar'desh needs two elemental signets. The earthen signet is held by Gruul the Dragonkiller in his lair in the Blade's Edge Mountains. The other, the blazing signet, is the burning heart of Nightbane, a mythical beast said to dwell in the hallowed halls of the prophet Medivh.
sources: quests 10901 and 13431 description (identical: the earthen signet held by Gruul the Dragonkiller in his lair in the Blade's Edge Mountains; the blazing heart of Nightbane in the hallowed halls of the prophet, Medivh)

parts.body: With both signets in his hands, Skar'this swore that the reformed cudgel would break his bonds, and that he would return to Serpentshrine to take vengeance on Vashj and her minions. He had not forgotten their agreement, he said: his ally, too, would now be able to enter the lair of Lady Vashj.
sources: quest 10901 completion text (With the cudgel reformed, I shall break free of my bonds and return to Serpentshrine to exact vengeance on Vashj and her minions!) and reward text (I have not forgotten our agreement, mortal. You too will now be able to enter the lair of Lady Vashj.)

parts.body: With both signets in his hands, Skar'this swore that the reformed cudgel would break his bonds, and that he would return to Serpentshrine to take vengeance on Vashj and her minions. At last, he said: with his bonds broken and the cudgel his, he would send the sea witch back to the icy depths.
sources: quest 13431 completion text (same as 10901) and reward text (With these bonds broken and the cudgel in my possession I shall send the sea witch back to the icy depths...)

notes: Placed in the Slave Pens file, not Serpentshrine's: 10900, 10901 and 13431 are filed under QuestSortID 3717 and are given and ended by Skar'this in the Slave Pens, so the storyline ends here (check_staged also rejects another instance's sort). Entry requiredState 8 like the rest of the Slave Pens; Serpentshrine is named only as his goal. Opening on DONE 10900 (QuestType 0, auto-complete, so DONE only; started and ended by 22421 with or without the module) and ACCEPT 10901 / 13431. Without mod-individual-progression Skar'this gives 13431 (10901 has no starter and is disabled); with it he gives 10901 (the attunement) and 13431 loses its starter and ender. Part 1 is the text both share; part 2 on DONE 10901 carries the module's reward (the way into Vashj's lair, true only where 10901 exists); part 3 on DONE 13431 the base reward. Each part is true for its own trigger, so the entry reads right with and without the module. No difficulty is named (the log text's 'heroic Slave Pens' is left out). Skar'this the Summoner 40446 (Midsummer, Ahune) is a different creature and is not used. The meaning of Kar'desh is not explained (no period text does); it is not tied to Nagrand's totem of Kar'dash. Check: opening's Neptulon line brought closer to 10900's reward text. Part 2 now gives the way into Vashj's lair as Skar'this's word, since with the module the raid also needs state 9. Both readings checked: base (13431 given and ended by 22421, 10901 disabled and starterless) and module (dungeon_attunements.sql: 10901 given and ended by 22421, QuestType 2, disable lifted; 13431 loses starter and ender); 10900 auto-complete (QuestType 0) and DONE only in both; nothing needs state 9 (Gruul and Karazhan are state 8).
